subject.title: [Feature]: Reusable gateway WebSocket client SDK package

question: Should OpenClaw publish and support a low-level `@openclaw/gateway-client` WebSocket SDK, or keep third-party clients on Gateway RPC docs and the higher-level app SDK path for now?
rationale: Current main has private implementation groundwork, but publication would create a new external auth, pairing, scope, token-storage, reconnect, transport, and compatibility contract that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Keep this as the SDK direction packet
options.body: Use this issue to decide the supported low-level client boundary before publishing it or redirecting the request to the higher-level SDK track.

options.title: Fold into the app SDK track
options.body: Close or redirect this only after maintainers decide external clients should use the higher-level SDK/Gateway RPC path and preserve the low-level requirements there.

options.title: Sponsor public gateway-client publication
options.body: Move toward publication with package metadata, install docs, Node/browser support boundaries, security guidance, compatibility tests, and live Gateway pairing proof.

recommendation.title: Keep this as the SDK direction packet
recommendation.body: Use this issue to decide the supported low-level client boundary before publishing it or redirecting the request to the higher-level SDK track.

likelyOwner.reason: The private package extraction and host-wrapper boundary most directly trace to steipete's merged gateway-client package work.
